candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: T-20260929-01's queue task asks for a re-judgment of H-20260924-01's 6 rules under K1/K2 (next-open fill, S3-relative bar) instead of a repeat of G1-G5.

objective: Re-judge H-20260924-01's 6 published ETF dip-reversion rules (registry dir:etf_dip_reversion_ibs_connors) on SPY/QQQ 1x under this project's frozen K1/K2 screening-lane contract (10bp/20bp, close signal -> next open fill), for scripts/screen_batch.py --batch h20260929_01_dip_rejudge --iteration h20260929_01_dip_rejudge. No return, Sharpe or backtest number is computed in this dossier.

sources.core_claim: IBS (close position within the day's own high-low range) forecasts next-day close-to-close ETF returns: 0.35% mean return after IBS<0.20 vs -0.13% after IBS>0.80, attributed to intraday overreaction corrected the next day.
sources.project_applicability: Primary source and formula for D2 and the IBS component of D1/D6; grounds the family's mechanism per the owner's requirement to justify pure technical rules by mechanism.
sources.reflection: Sample ends 2013-05-12, entirely pre-dating this iteration's windows; author states IBS alone is cost-eroded, hence the filter/trend-filter variants D1/D3/D4/D5/D6. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Filtering a Cutler's RSI(3) mean-reversion strategy to require IBS<=0.5 removes ~43% of days in market while raising total return 9.6% on average across the ETF sample.
sources.project_applicability: Direct precedent for D6 (IBS-filtered RSI(2)), the combination this iteration's engine actually implements with tighter, disclosed thresholds.
sources.reflection: Uses RSI(3)/IBS<=0.5, not this iteration's RSI(2)<=5/IBS<0.20; the improvement size for the exact D4/D6 parameterization is untested by the paper. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Connors' RSI(2) strategy: 200-day SMA trend filter, buy when 2-period RSI moves below 10 (deeply oversold).
sources.project_applicability: Exact entry rule for D4 (RSI(2)<=5 used here) and, with the IBS filter, D6.
sources.reflection: Secondary educational reference; StockCharts explicitly disclaims it as an out-of-the-box standalone system. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Connors exits long positions on a move above the 5-day SMA.
sources.project_applicability: Exact exit rule for D4 and D6.
sources.reflection: Same secondary-source caveat as the entry-rule claim. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Weekly 'winners'/'losers' show sizeable return reversals the next week that persist as apparent arbitrage profits after thin-trading, bid-ask and cost adjustments.
sources.project_applicability: Independent, pre-Pagonidis academic grounding for the short-horizon overreaction/reversal mechanism this whole family relies on.
sources.reflection: Weekly horizon, equities not ETFs, 1988/1990 vintage; does not test IBS, RSI(2) or any ETF rule directly. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Kloßner, Becker & Friedmann model stock prices with a fundamental process plus a news-impact curve, deriving OHLC-based statistics that separately measure upside/downside intraday overreaction, with a 'buy on bad news' strategy illustrating the economic significance.
sources.project_applicability: Directly cited by Pagonidis (2014) as the closest academic treatment of intraday overreaction, the mechanism this family's IBS and RSI(2) rules exploit.
sources.reflection: ScienceDirect full text returned 403 this session; only the IDEAS/RePEc abstract page was opened, not the paper itself. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Pandey & Joshi investigate IBS as a key indicator for trading a bucket of country ETFs over a 10-year period, a post-2013 continuation of academic interest in the IBS effect.
sources.project_applicability: Shows the IBS effect remains an active research topic after Pagonidis's 2013-05 sample cutoff, though on foreign country ETFs rather than the US index ETFs this iteration tests.
sources.reflection: Tests country ETFs, the case Pagonidis himself found much weaker or absent outside the US; not a direct confirmation of the US-only effect this iteration relies on. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: Algotradekit's Pine source for QQQ/SPY: IBS<=0.09/0.11 with EMA(220)/EMA(200) trend filter, exit IBS>=0.985/0.995 or a max trade duration (14 days for QQQ, 12 for SPY in the source's own comment).
sources.project_applicability: Primary implementation source for D1, read directly from the local fmzquant/strategies git clone (commit 7853bb2, per I-20260923-10) rather than paraphrased from the marketing description.
sources.reflection: IBS is computed from the prior completed bar with process_orders_on_close=false, an extra-lag idiom this iteration's engine deliberately does not reproduce (see decision-record.md); SPY's published max-hold is 12, not the 14 this iteration uses per the frozen task brief. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: R3 ETF Strategy Pine source: close>EMA(200), RSI(2) three sessions ago <60, RSI(2) falling three sessions in a row, RSI(2) today <10; exit on RSI(2) crossing above 70.
sources.project_applicability: Primary implementation source for D3 (Connors & Alvarez 2009 'R3'), read directly from the local git clone; uses today's own OHLC (no prior-bar lag issue), next-open fill.
sources.reflection: No stated performance numbers on the page; a bare Pine port with no backtest evidence attached. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

sources.core_claim: ETF 3-Day Reversion Strategy Pine source: close>EMA(200), close<EMA(5), three consecutive lower highs and lower lows; exit on close crossing above EMA(5); process_orders_on_close=true (same-close fill).
sources.project_applicability: Primary implementation source for D5 (Connors & Alvarez 2009 '3-Day High/Low'), read directly from the local git clone; its own backtest convention is the same-close fill this iteration's T0 diagnostic reproduces and flags as unexecutable.
sources.reflection: No stated performance numbers on the page; same-close fill is optimistic versus any realistic execution. [Reused verbatim for h20260929_01_dip_rejudge, 2026-09-29: same rule family, evidence not re-fetched -- only the keep bar and fill-timing framing changed, see decision above.]

existing_solution_comparison: H-20260924-01 (2026-09-24) already tested these exact 6 rules (D1-D6) on QQQ/SPY 1x/3x under the giants-sweep G1-G5 protocol at T0 (same-close, unexecutable upper bound) and T2 (next-open, the same fill timing this batch uses) -- 0/24 candidates passed G1/G1' at either timing; D1 additionally failed its own preregistered random-entry-timing placebo (real percentile 58-92 across cells, needs >=95). This iteration reuses that same rule set and evidence base verbatim (no new source is opened); the only change is the KEEP BAR (K1/K2 vs S3, this project's 2026-09-28 owner-set bar) and the addition of the 2016-2023 stress window, which H-20260924-01 never tested (its own WARMUP_START was 2022-06-01). Per the mission's reuse-before-repeat rule, this is a re-judgment under a different bar, not a repeat of an already-answered question -- the queue task (T-20260929-01, 2026-09-29 02:1x coordinator revision) explicitly asks for this re-judgment because K1/K2 is a materially different (softer on CAGR, relative-to-S3) bar than G1/G1', so the prior refutation does not automatically resolve this question.
negative_experiments_checked: H-20260924-01's own sleeve-level refutation (0/24 at G1/G1', deflated Sharpe 0.92 for the best T0 cell given 24 trials) and D1's placebo failure are the direct prior; this iteration checks whether the softer, S3-relative K1/K2 bar changes that verdict, not whether the rules are 'good' in absolute terms. h20260928_42_opex_week's refutation (another calendar/flow-adjacent mechanism, 0/8 primary, negative anchor Sharpe on all 8) sets the recent-round base rate for this kind of re-judgment: most published rules fail K1/K2 under this project's specific 10bp/20bp next-open-fill contract even when an academic mechanism is real.
